title: Rate against substrate concentration
caption: At low substrate concentration the rate rises steeply; at high concentration every active site is busy and the rate levels off at Vmax. Km is the substrate concentration at which the rate is half of Vmax: here 2 mmol per dm³.
alt: A curve of reaction rate against substrate concentration rising steeply and levelling towards a dashed Vmax of 100, with the rate of 50 marked at a concentration of 2.
description: The curve starts at the origin and rises steeply: more substrate, more collisions with active sites.
It flattens as the active sites become saturated, approaching Vmax = 100.
Half of Vmax, 50, is reached at a substrate concentration of 2 mmol per dm³. This is Km.

checks.name: at [S] = Km = 2 the rate is half of Vmax: v = 50
at [S] = 20, ten times Km, the rate is within 10% of Vmax
at low [S] the rate rises in proportion to [S]: gradient Vmax ÷ Km = 50
